metadata.title: Dog Days Are Never Over
metadata.description: You are a dog. Five bones are missing from your basket. Find them around the neighborhood and carry them home one at a time.

deathMessage: You curl up somewhere safe. The neighborhood can wait until tomorrow.

rooms.name: Backyard
rooms.description: Your yard smells like dry grass and home, but something is wrong. The wicker basket beside your bed is empty. All five of your favorite bones are gone. The loose gate stands open to the east.
rooms.shortDescription: Home again: bed, water, and the basket waiting for its five bones.

rooms.name: Side Yard
rooms.description: A strip of packed dirt runs between the house and hedge. The hose has slumped across the path. Leaves bunch under the rattling gate, holding yesterday's smells.
rooms.shortDescription: The narrow side yard runs between hedge and house.

rooms.name: Front Porch
rooms.description: Painted steps overlook Maple Street. One corner of the welcome mat refuses to lie flat. A parcel sits by the front door.

rooms.name: Maple Street
rooms.description: Maple Street smells of hot pavement and old tire tracks. The cul-de-sac is north, the park is south, and home is west.
rooms.shortDescription: Maple Street links home, the cul-de-sac, and the park.

rooms.name: Cul-de-sac
rooms.description: The street ends in a broad circle. Chalk covers the pavement. A sprinkler ticks across one lawn, and a beagle watches through the fence.
rooms.shortDescription: A sunny road circle with chalk, sprinkler, and a watching dog.

rooms.name: Pocket Park
rooms.description: An oak shades the patchy lawn. A squirrel works at the roots with both paws and keeps glancing at you. The creek path runs east; the community garden is south.
rooms.shortDescription: The pocket park is shaded by one squirrel-occupied oak.

rooms.name: Creek Path
rooms.description: Creek water moves over pebbles beside the dirt path. A duck holds the middle. Something familiar smells from under a length of driftwood.
rooms.shortDescription: Water chatters beside the creek path.

rooms.name: Community Garden
rooms.description: Tomato vines lean over the raised beds. One patch of soil is softer than the rest. The compost bin smells so strong it blots out everything downwind.
rooms.shortDescription: Raised beds and rich smells fill the community garden.

rooms.name: Service Alley
rooms.description: The alley runs behind garages and tall fences. A trash can leans toward the pavement. A cat sits on a sagging crate and watches you arrive.
rooms.shortDescription: The alley is a corridor of bins, fences, and concentrated smells.

presentation.listingText: An empty wicker basket waits beside the bed.

examine.text: Your bone basket can hold all five missing treasures. Put each recovered bone in the basket.

presentation.listingText: Your water bowl glints near the house.

examine.text: A broad metal bowl full of clean water. The surface trembles when you breathe on it.

presentation.listingText: Your flattened bed occupies the warmest patch.

examine.text: It holds a deep reserve of your own warm smell.

presentation.listingText: A faded tennis ball rests in the grass.

examine.text: Soft on one side and carrying the ghosts of many games.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: Warm fence boards enclose the yard.

examine.text: Every board holds a different message from rain, squirrels, and neighboring dogs.

presentation.listingText: A green hose lies in a loose coil.

examine.text: It smells faintly of rubber and cold water.

presentation.listingText: A thick hedge crowds the path.

examine.text: A sparrow feather is caught between two leaves. Near the ground, narrow trails disappear under the fence.

presentation.listingText: The loose gate rattles in the breeze.

examine.text: The latch is high, but the gate already stands open enough for a dog.

presentation.listingText: A knotted rope has been forgotten beneath the hedge.

examine.text: One knot is wet. You do not remember leaving it under the hedge.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A stiff welcome mat guards the front door.

examine.text: The mat is slightly raised at one corner. Something familiar is trapped beneath it.

presentation.listingText: The closed front door smells reassuringly of home.

examine.text: You know this door well. Today the neighborhood is on this side of it.

presentation.listingText: A small parcel waits by the door.

examine.text: Cardboard, tape, van tires, and no obvious food.

behaviors.openMessage: You worry a loose flap open. It contains only packing paper.
behaviors.closeMessage: You nose the flap shut again.

presentation.listingText: The squeaky bone lies exposed beside the mat.

examine.text: Your yellow squeaky bone, flattened in the middle but still capable of one heroic squeak.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A red hydrant stands at the curb.

examine.text: Official paint covers a dense archive of unofficial dog messages.

presentation.listingText: A delivery van cools beside the curb.

examine.text: Its tires carry the smell of dozens of streets and one sandwich shop.

presentation.listingText: A storm drain breathes damp air from below.

examine.text: Wet leaves are packed under the grate. Air moves below, but your head will not fit.

presentation.listingText: A paper bag skitters whenever the breeze catches it.

examine.text: The bottom is torn out. It still jumps every time the wind catches it.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A friendly beagle watches through a low fence.

examine.text: A beagle with a white muzzle pushes his nose through the fence. His collar tag taps the boards.

presentation.listingText: A sprinkler ticks bright water across the grass.

examine.text: Every sweep promises either a drink or a soaking.

presentation.listingText: Chalk loops and squares cover the pavement.

examine.text: Children have drawn suns, monsters, and something that may be a dog.

presentation.listingText: An excellent stick lies beside the curb.

examine.text: Straight enough to carry, crooked enough to be interesting, and exactly the right weight.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A squirrel patrols the oak roots.

examine.text: Its front paws never stop moving. It watches you without turning its head.

presentation.listingText: An old oak spreads shade over the lawn.

examine.text: Its bark records generations of claws, rain, insects, and squirrel arrogance.

presentation.listingText: A wooden bench faces the grass.

examine.text: It smells of sun, old lunches, and many different trousers.

presentation.listingText: Patchy grass invites a good roll.

examine.text: Cool blades, dry soil, clover, and several trails worth following.

presentation.listingText: The red rubber bone has fallen from the oak roots.

examine.text: A red rubber bone with tiny squirrel tooth marks. The insult is almost impressive.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A shallow creek chatters beside the path.

examine.text: Cold water curls over pebbles and carries news from upstream.

presentation.listingText: A length of driftwood blocks a familiar smell.

examine.text: The wood is light enough to nudge. Something bone-like is wedged beneath it.

presentation.listingText: Tall reeds tremble at the water's edge.

examine.text: A frog drops into the water before you see it. The reeds also smell faintly of an old tennis ball.

presentation.listingText: A duck watches you from the creek.

examine.text: It drifts sideways whenever you look at it, keeping the same patch of water between you.

presentation.listingText: The blue nylon bone rests where the driftwood was.

examine.text: A blue nylon bone polished by creek water but unmistakably yours.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: One patch of soft soil has already been disturbed.

examine.text: Someone turned this patch recently. Under the tomato roots is a smell you know.

presentation.listingText: A compost bin hums with forbidden perfume.

examine.text: The lid leaks a warm, sour smell. You could spend all afternoon sorting it out.

behaviors.openMessage: You nose the lid up. The smell is magnificent, but there is nothing safe to eat.
behaviors.closeMessage: You bump the compost lid closed.

presentation.listingText: Tomato vines lean over a raised bed.

examine.text: Green stems, warm fruit, and the faint paw-smell of a rabbit.

presentation.listingText: A rabbit freezes between two planters.

examine.text: Its body is still. Its nose is not. It knows exactly where the fence gap is.

presentation.listingText: The striped rawhide bone protrudes from the loosened soil.

examine.text: A striped rawhide bone, earthy but intact. You remember burying it and regret nothing.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A tilted trash can promises terrible decisions.

examine.text: The lid sits crooked. Beneath the ordinary garbage smells is the unmistakable scent of your oldest bone.

behaviors.openMessage: You nose the lid aside. A wall of glorious smells rolls out.
behaviors.closeMessage: With surprising responsibility, you push the lid closed.

presentation.listingText: A soft cardboard crate sags near a garage.

examine.text: It once held oranges. Now it holds dust and several excellent claw marks.

behaviors.openMessage: You pull open a damp flap. Nothing inside but old paper.
behaviors.closeMessage: You fold the flap down again.

presentation.listingText: An alley cat watches from the crate.

examine.text: The cat's ears tip back. One hind paw is already braced against the crate.

presentation.listingText: A rainbow-edged puddle fills a pothole.

examine.text: It smells wrong for drinking but extremely available for stepping in.

presentation.listingText: The old white bone is visible inside the open trash can.

examine.text: Your oldest white bone, scarred by years of serious chewing.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

presentation.listingText: A dog biscuit is tucked beneath the packing paper.

examine.text: A small biscuit shaped like a bone. Its smell occupies your complete attention.

behaviors.blockedMessage: Your mouth is already full. Drop what you are carrying first.

commands.name: List exits
commands.helpDescription: Show directions you can currently travel.

effects.message: That's not a direction you can go.
You can't go that way.

commands.name: Face
commands.helpDescription: Turn to face an absolute or relative direction without moving.

effects.message: That's not a direction you can face.
You turn to face the {variable face-direction name}.
You can't take that.
You can't take that right now.

commands.name: Drop
commands.helpDescription: Put down an item you are carrying.

effects.message: You can't drop that.
You can't examine that.
You can't open that.
You can't close that.
You can't lock that.
You can't unlock that.
You can't use that.

commands.name: Use with target
commands.helpDescription: Use one accessible item with another.

effects.message: You can't use that.
You can't use it on that.

commands.name: Put inside
commands.helpDescription: Place a carried item inside a container.

effects.message: You can't put that anywhere.
You can't put it in that.

commands.name: Put on
commands.helpDescription: Place a carried item on a surface.

effects.message: You can't put that anywhere.
You can't put it on that.

commands.name: Inventory
commands.helpDescription: List what you are carrying in your mouth.

effects.emptyMessage: Your mouth is empty. You can carry one ordinary object at a time.

commands.name: Sniff around
commands.helpDescription: Investigate the scents in your current location.

messages: You lower your nose and sort through the neighborhood: warm dirt, old rain, grass, and several promising mysteries.
Your nose maps the area more clearly than eyes ever could. Nothing urgent, but almost everything is interesting.
You take a long, serious sniff. The air is crowded with stories, most of them involving food or feet.

commands.name: Sniff something
commands.helpDescription: Inspect an item, animal, or landmark by scent.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: The {variable dog-sniff-target-target name} smells alive, alert, and full of private information.
You exchange a dense packet of scent-information with the {variable dog-sniff-target-target name}. No words are needed.
The {variable dog-sniff-target-target name} smells edible. This is the highest praise you can give anything.
The scent of the {variable dog-sniff-target-target name} is cool, damp, and drinkable.
The scent beneath the {variable dog-sniff-target-target name} is layered and complicated. Digging could change that.
You sniff the {variable dog-sniff-target-target name} from several angles. It now belongs to the part of the world you understand.
The {variable dog-sniff-target-target name} has a distinct smell. You commit it to memory.
WOOF! The sound travels farther than expected. Somewhere, another dog answers.
You bark with conviction. The neighborhood has been properly informed.
One sharp bark. A bird leaves a nearby roof, which feels like a measurable success.

commands.name: Bark at something
commands.helpDescription: Direct a bark at an item or animal.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You bark at the {variable dog-bark-at-target name}. The situation is now louder and no clearer.
WOOF! The {variable dog-bark-at-target name} has received your formal notice.
You bark at the {variable dog-bark-at-target name}. It does not retreat, but you remain vigilant.
You bark at the {variable dog-bark-at-target name}. It refuses to explain itself.
A forceful bark changes nothing about the {variable dog-bark-at-target name}, except perhaps its reputation.
Your tail thumps out a cheerful rhythm.
You wag hard enough to involve your whole back half.
Your tail reports that conditions are acceptable.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You wag at the {variable dog-wag-at-target name}, making your peaceful intentions extremely obvious.
You wag at the {variable dog-wag-at-target name}. Friendliness costs nothing.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You give the {variable dog-lick-target name} one quick, socially informative lick.
One lick confirms that the {variable dog-lick-target name} deserves further attention.
The {variable dog-lick-target name} tastes cold, metallic, and disappointingly inedible.
You lick the {variable dog-lick-target name}. This answers one question and raises another.
The {variable dog-lick-target name} does not taste the way it looks.

commands.name: Nudge
commands.helpDescription: Push something experimentally with your nose.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You nudge the {variable dog-nudge-target name} with your nose: a gentle but unmistakable request for attention.
You nudge the {variable dog-nudge-target name}. It shifts just enough to reward the experiment.
A firm nose-push establishes that the {variable dog-nudge-target name} is real and currently in your way.

commands.name: Paw or scratch
commands.helpDescription: Paw or scratch at something reachable.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: Your claws rake through the {variable dog-paw-target name}. A proper excavation would require digging.
You paw insistently at the {variable dog-paw-target name}. It receives several new claw marks.
Scratch, scratch, scratch. The {variable dog-paw-target name} remains stubbornly itself.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You chew the {variable dog-chew-target name} with focused satisfaction.
The {variable dog-chew-target name} squeaks or creaks under your teeth. Excellent.
You decide not to bite the {variable dog-chew-target name}. A warning huff will do.
Your teeth meet the {variable dog-chew-target name}. Metal wins this round.
You give the {variable dog-chew-target name} a thoughtful experimental chew.
The {variable dog-chew-target name} has poor mouthfeel but useful structural information.

commands.name: Dig
commands.helpDescription: Dig at something marked as diggable.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: Dirt flies behind you as you dig into the {variable dog-dig-target name}. The ground is now thoroughly disturbed.
You dig with all four paws and very little concern for landscaping. The {variable dog-dig-target name} will never be the same.

commands.name: Chase
commands.helpDescription: Pursue an animal or moving object.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You spring after the {variable dog-chase-target name}! It escapes for now, but the chase itself was magnificent.
You chase the {variable dog-chase-target name} in a fast, untidy loop before it gets away.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You pounce on the {variable dog-play-target name}, toss it, catch it badly, and declare the game a success.
For several glorious seconds, the {variable dog-play-target name} becomes the center of the universe.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You lap noisily from the {variable dog-drink-target name}. Water goes into your mouth and also everywhere else.
A long drink from the {variable dog-drink-target name} leaves your muzzle dripping.

commands.name: Roll in something
commands.helpDescription: Roll in something that invites poor decisions.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You drop a shoulder and roll enthusiastically in the {variable dog-roll-target name}. You emerge transformed in ways humans may not appreciate.
Back, side, other side, vigorous wriggle. The {variable dog-roll-target name} is now part of your personal scent.

commands.name: Mark
commands.helpDescription: Leave your scent on a reachable landmark.

effects.message: You cannot find anything like that here.

messages: You consider marking the {variable dog-mark-target name}, then choose diplomacy instead.
You mark the {variable dog-mark-target name}. Any dog with a working nose will understand the announcement.
A brief, businesslike pause establishes your opinion of the {variable dog-mark-target name}.

effects.message: You cannot find anything edible like that here.

messages: You eat the {variable dog-eat-target name}. No crumbs survive.
The {variable dog-eat-target name} disappears in two bites and one optimistic gulp.

commands.name: Give
commands.helpDescription: Offer a carried item to an animal.

effects.message: You do not have anything like that to give.
There is no such animal here.
You set the {variable dog-give-item name} down in front of the {variable dog-give-target name} and wait hopefully.
You need to be carrying the {variable dog-give-item name} before you can offer it.

commands.name: Sit
commands.helpDescription: Sit politely, or at least convincingly.

messages: You sit neatly, radiating the expectation of a reward.
You sit. This is exceptionally good work.

commands.name: Lie down
commands.helpDescription: Settle onto the ground without ending the adventure.

messages: You fold onto the ground with a long, satisfied sigh.
You lie down while remaining ready to leap up for anything important.
You turn around twice, curl up, and steal a compact but excellent nap.
You close your eyes for a moment. Neighborhood smells continue without supervision.
You wait for a moment, alert to anything that might happen.
You stay put. Time passes, along with at least one interesting smell.
A long howl rises over the fences. Far away, another voice joins for one wavering note.
You howl from the deepest part of yourself. The suburb briefly belongs to the song.
A low warning rumbles in your chest.
You produce a serious growl, just in case seriousness is needed.
You release a small, devastatingly persuasive whine.
Your whine suggests that nobody has ever understood hunger or loneliness as deeply as you do now.
You spring straight up and land with unnecessary force.
Four paws leave the ground. For a moment, gravity loses track of you.
You shake from nose to tail, ears flapping like loose laundry.
A full-body shake restores every hair to a slightly different position.
Front legs long, chest low, tail high: a complete and excellent stretch.
You stretch until your paws spread and your back gives a tiny satisfied shiver.

commands.name: Listen
commands.helpDescription: Attend carefully to the sounds around you.

messages: You hold perfectly still. Leaves scrape, pipes hum, claws click somewhere beyond a fence.
Your ears swivel independently through the small sounds of the neighborhood.
You attack an itch with one back foot until it retreats.
Scratch scratch scratch. Balance becomes briefly theoretical.
You find a suitable spot and do what dogs have always done. Someone else can worry about the bag.
You conduct a brief and private transaction with the lawn.

commands.name: Goal
commands.helpDescription: Review the missing-bones goal and how to win.

effects.message: Five favorite bones are missing. Search the porch, alley, park, creek path, and community garden. Carry them home one at a time and put each bone in the backyard basket. Examine the basket whenever you want to check its contents.
Your nose flips the mat's raised corner. There is your squeaky bone, flattened but safe.
The squirrel rockets up the oak and drops something red from between the roots: your rubber bone.
The driftwood rolls aside. Creek water flashes around your blue nylon bone.
Your paws strike something solid. A striped rawhide bone pushes out of the loose soil.
The beagle answers with two bright barks, then races one delighted lap along the fence. You have exchanged all essential information.
The sprinkler clicks around while you drink and catches you squarely behind the ears. You are refreshed, betrayed, and dripping.
A distant bark acknowledges your update to the hydrant. The neighborhood record is current again.
The duck paddles exactly three feet farther away and resumes judging you. Technically, you drove it back.
The cat vaults to the fence, lets you thunder underneath, and returns to the crate the instant your back is turned.
You rise wearing an impressive rainbow sheen. This will be difficult to explain and even harder to regret.

All five bones are home in the basket! You circle twice, collapse beside your complete collection, and thump your tail against the floorboards. You win — and the neighborhood remains open for further mischief.

messages: A lawn mower starts somewhere beyond the fences, then fades behind a row of houses.
A car door slams two streets away. Your ears turn before the rest of you does.
The breeze brings charcoal smoke, cut grass, and the possible existence of sausages.
A distant dog barks once. You store the information for later.
A bird scolds the neighborhood from a power line.
Somewhere nearby, a mail slot claps shut.
